To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the periplasm of E. coli is a suitable compartment for production of heterologous recombinant proteins and that the outer membrane and extracellular space of E. coli are useful compartments for the display of heterologous polypeptides on the bacterial surface.

(a) a combination of a signal peptide and a specific chaperone can be used to direct a heterologous protein into the periplasm or outer membrane of E. coli, (b) a signal peptide can also be used to direct heterologous proteins to the surface of E. coli or to secrete the heterologous proteins into the culture medium, (c) a combination of signal peptide and chaperone can also be used for secretion of the heterologous protein,

(1) The periplasm is a good place for production of heterologous enzymes and proteins, (2) Outer membrane display of functional proteins is feasible, (3) Secretion of functional heterologous proteins is also possible and (4) The extracellular space is a good compartment for production of functional heterologously expressed antibodies.
